cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Admit It Wasn’t Fair
cards.instruction: Get an apology that acknowledges how the rules, comparison, or outcome worked against you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crouched when you crouched, and everyone ran past us. You owe me an apology for that start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was tying my shoe. The starter had already fired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, checking equipment. You should apologize for giving me the wrong starting signal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't give a signal. I missed the start too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologize for passing your bad start on to me. I could have been running.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies crouching as a start cue; B2 reveals shoelace tying. A3 blames a wrong signal and A5 seeks acknowledgment that B's bad start cost A a chance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 shoe explanation becomes A3 equipment cover; B4 also missed start changes A5 blame to transmitting that disadvantage.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains and B4 asserts equal misfortune, plausibly resisting responsibility.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 shared failure to demand a more specific apology, not just repeat signal blame.

specificity.evidence: A1 other runners pass and B2 fired starter make the missed-race stakes clear.
